The Best Chili Recipe

Published October 20, 2026. Updated October 28, 2026

This post may contain affiliate links. Read our disclosure policy.

  • Jump to Recipe

My idea of the BEST Homemade Chili Recipe! Slow simmered on the stovetop and made with plenty of hearty beef, earthy chili spices, sweet crushed tomatoes and bell peppers, all in a rich dense broth. It’s an excellent recipe for fall festivities, game day, cozy home cooked dinners, and chili cook offs!

Over the years I’ve shared many ways to make chili including healthier versions such as Vegetarian Chili, Quinoa Chili, Sweet Potato and Black Bean Chili. A traditional Chili Con Carne and a Turkey Chili. A fun spin making Chili Mac, plus my highly popular White Chicken Chili and Slow Cooker Chili.

But what I’ve been missing is one I think you’ll turn to most often, this flavor packed, stovetop cooked, classic chili. This is the batch of chili that will have you savoring every bite!

Chili was one of the very first things I learned to cook. I was actually the kid that would go to the library and read the cookbooks instead of the fiction books.

I remember learning to cook chili from a Betty Crocker cookbook and ever since I’ve made hundreds of batches of chili many different ways. This recipe is my favorite I’ve come up with.

It’s straightforward, covers all the bases, has rich depth of flavor, and it’s a chili everyone can agree on. It freezes beautifully and it’s excellent over baked potatoes if you want it even heartier.

I’d dare say this is the ultimate cold weather stew. Try it soon and pile it high with all your favorite chili toppings!

Homemade Chili Recipe Ingredients

Oil: Use olive oil or avocado oil to brown the beef.

Ground beef: I recommend 85% lean ground beef. It’s not too fatty but fatty enough it will brown up nicely and be tender.

Sugar: This is used to help brown the meat better, and it balances the acidity of the tomatoes. Two for one.

Salt and black pepper: Salt brings out all the other flavors, pepper adds a little background depth.

Red bell pepper: This adds natural sweetness that isn’t overpowering as well as some bright flavor.

Yellow onion and garlic: Staple ingredients to chili to build up its foundational flavors.

Spices: You’ll need mild chili powder, ancho chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, and coriander.

Alcohol: Use either pale lager beer, pinot noir red wine or vodka. If you prefer not to cook with alcohol at all that’s fine simply replace with more broth just note that the flavor won’t have quite the same depth.

Crushed tomatoes: Canned San Marzano or Roma (Plum) tomatoes are best here for their natural sweetness and less acidity than a standard generic canned tomato.

Canned green chilies: These Hatch chilies adds some southwestern flavor to the chili.

Broth: Use low-sodium chicken broth or beef broth. Homemade broth will offer the absolute best flavor (I always keep some stashed in the freezer).

Beef base: This isn’t a must if you don’t have it but it does boost the flavor a bit.

Cocoa powder: A little of this goes a long ways in chili to add that secret ingredient flavor.

Mexican oregano: You can find this in the Latin foods section of grocery stores or online.

Canned kidney beans and pinto beans: Using two types adds a variation of flavor and color.

Toppings of choice (see ideas below).

How to Make Chili on the Stovetop

Preheat pot: Heat olive oil in a pot over medium-high heat.

Brown the beef: Dab beef dry with paper towels and season both sides of beef lightly with the sugar and a few pinches of salt. Break beef into 6 chunks. Place beef in pot and lightly press down for good contact. Let cook until nicely browned on bottom about 3 minutes.

Turn beef and cook about 2 to 3 minutes then continue to break up and cook beef through. Transfer beef to a plate lined with paper towels and leave about 1 1/2 Tbsp rendered fat in pot.

Saute vegetables: Carefully add bell peppers to pot (the fat can splatter). Let cook without moving about 3 minutes to get some color on them. Reduce heat to medium, add onions and cook tossing occasionally 5 minutes.

Bloom spices: Add in chili powder, ancho chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander and black pepper to taste. Saute 10 seconds.

Add liquids, remaining seasonings: Pour in beer (wine or vodka) while stirring and scraping up browned bits from bottom of pot. Pour in 1 cup broth, tomatoes, and green chilies. Add beef base, cocoa powder and oregano.

Return cooked ground beef. Stir mixture and bring to a simmer.

Simmer low and slow: Reduce heat to a gentle simmer (medium-low to low depending on your burner size), cover pot and let simmer 30 to 60 minutes stirring occasionally. Add more broth as needed to thin chili to desired consistency.

Add beans: Stir in kidney beans and pinto beans during the last 15 minutes of cooking.

Cool and garnish: Let chili cool slightly and serve with toppings of choice.

Topping Ideas for Chili

There are so many ways to finish chili, pick a few of your favorite:

Cheese: Cheddar cheese, Monterey Jack, Pepper Jack, Queso Fresco, Cotija, or Smoked Gouda. A good choice to add a tang that compliments the chili.

Vegetables or fruits: Red onion, jalapenos, fresh tomatoes, radishes, corn, avocado, limes or oranges for spritzing. These will add more fresh flavor.

Greens: Green onions, cilantro or chives. You’ll find these are great as a garnish for color and to brighten the overall flavor.

Chips/Crackers: Tortilla chips, fritos, saltine crackers or oyster crackers. Excellent choices for a crisp texture contrast to the smooth broth and chewy fillers of the chili.

Condiments: Sour cream, Greek yogurt, crème fraîche or guacamole. A creamy fat cuts through and balances the acidity.

Breads: Cornbread or croutons. These are nice for additional flavor and texture.

Meats: Cooked bacon or chorizo. If you want even more meat flavor and protein boost your chili with one of these.

Helpful Tips for the Best Chili

Brown the beef well: One of the most important tips for a good chili is to really allow the ground beef to sear and get some browning going on. Drying it beforehand and adding a little sugar also helps assist in this. Browned ground beef boosts to overall flavor of the chili dramatically vs. over-stirring it and only cooking it through. If time allows you may even opt to cook the beef in two batches if you want even more browning.

Use quality ingredients: The chili will only taste as good as the ingredients you put into, so I recommend things like fresh ground beef from the butcher (vs. using pre-packaged chubs), homemade broth if possible, and high quality canned tomatoes.

Simmer low and slow: To really develop the overall flavor of chili let simmer for an extended period of time over a low heat. This also allows time for the flavors to meld together.

Mild chili powders: If serving this to people that don’t like spicy food make sample a dab of your chili powders to ensure they are both mild. If the ancho chili powder is a bit spicy for you, increase the standard chili powder to 3 Tbsp total.

Top it: We all know chili is better with cheddar. And any other toppings you love.

Possible Variations

Ground turkey chili: If you want a healthier meat option you can make this with lean ground turkey in place of ground beef.

Peppers: You can try other peppers here in place of bell pepper such as Poblano or Anaheim.

Add vegetables: If you want to add more nutrition try it with zucchini, carrots, or mushrooms.

Chili powder: This can be made with the standard generic chili powder or try other mild options such as New Mexico and California chili powder.

Bacon: I did test adding bacon directly to this chili and personally preferred the version without it added (surprisingly), but if you love a bacon kissed chili free to add a half pound (cooked) right to the pot of chili.

How to Store and Reheat Chili

Fridge storage: Cool chili slightly then store in an airtight container, chilled. It can keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

Freezer storage: For best quality, flavor and more nutrient retention homemade Chili can be kept frozen up to 3 months. Though you can extend longer than this up to 6 months just note the flavors mute slightly, textures degrade lightly and the vitamins (such as B and C) may not be as stable.

Thawing: Thaw frozen chili in the fridge for 1 to 2 days.

Microwave reheating: Single or double servings of chili can be reheated in the microwave in a microwave safe dish until warmed through (I recommend 50% power), stop and stir periodically during heating for even heating.

Stovetop reheating: Larger servings of chili can be rewarmed in a pot on the stovetop over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally for even heating. Add a splash of broth to thin it out as needed.

Slow cooker reheating: Note that slow cooker reheating is not recommended for any soup or stew including chili as this isn’t food safe. It takes too long for the chili to come up to a proper food safe temperature leaving it in the danger zone more prone to growing bacteria that could cause food borne illness.

What to Serve with Homemade Chili

Wondering what to pair with this delicious stew style dish? Try pairing it with one of these to make it more of a complete meal.

  • Apple Spinach Salad
  • Baked Potatoes
  • Classic Cornbread,  Southern Skillet Cornbread, or Pumpkin Cornbread
  • Classic Coleslaw or Apple Slaw
  • Mexican Street Corn (or buttered and salted corn on the cob, grilled or boiled)
  • Sweet Potato Fries or Russet French Fries
  • 1-Hour Dinner Rolls

Print Recipe

The Best Chili Recipe

This is my idea of the BEST Homemade Chili Recipe! Slow simmered on the stovetop and made with plenty of hearty beef, earthy chili spices, sweet crushed tomatoes and bell peppers, all in a rich dense broth. It's an excellent recipe for fall festivities, game day, cozy home cooked dinners, and chili cook offs! 
Servings: 7

Ingredients

  • 1 Tbsp olive oil or avocado oil
  • 1 3/4 lbs. 85% lean ground beef
  • 1 1/2 tsp sugar
  • Salt and black pepper, to taste
  • 1 1/4 cups chopped red bell pepper (1 medium)
  • 1 1/2 cups chopped yellow onion
  • 1 Tbsp minced garlic (3 cloves)
  • 2 Tbsp (14g) mild chili powder* (such as McCormick)
  • 1 Tbsp (7g) ancho chili powder
  • 1 Tbsp (5g) ground cumin
  • 2 tsp (6g) smoked paprika
  • 1 tsp (2g) ground coriander
  • 1/2 cup pale lager beer, pinot noir red wine, or 1/4 cup vodka**
  • 1 (29 oz) can crushed Roma tomatoes or San Marzano tomatoes in tomato puree
  • 1 (4 oz) can mild green chilies
  • 1 to 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth, homemade is best, or low-sodium beef broth
  • 2 tsp beef base
  • 1 1/2 tsp (3g) cocoa powder (regular unsweetened or Dutch)
  • 1 tsp (1g) Mexican oregano
  • 1 (15 oz) can dark red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
  • 1 (15 oz) can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
  • Toppings of choice, see notes

Instructions

  • Heat olive oil in a pot over medium-high heat.
  • Dab beef dry with paper towels and season both sides of beef lightly with the sugar and a few pinches of salt. Break beef into 6 chunks. Place beef in pot (flat side down) and lightly press down for good contact. Let cook until nicely browned on bottom about 3 minutes.
  • Turn beef and cook about 2 to 3 minutes then continue to break up and cook beef through. Transfer beef to a plate lined with paper towels and leave about 1 1/2 Tbsp rendered fat in pot.
  • Carefully add bell peppers to pot (the fat can splatter). Let cook without moving about 3 minutes to get some color on them. Reduce heat to medium, add onions and cook tossing occasionally 5 minutes.
  • Add garlic and saute 30 seconds.
  • Add in chili powder, ancho chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander and black pepper to taste. Saute 10 seconds.
  • Pour in beer (wine or vodka) while stirring and scraping up browned bits from bottom of pot. Pour in 1 cup broth, crushed tomatoes, and green chilies. Add beef base, cocoa powder, oregano and cooked ground beef. Stir mixture and bring to a simmer.
  • Reduce heat to a gentle simmer (medium-low to low depending on your burner size), cover pot and let simmer 30 to 60 minutes stirring occasionally. Add more broth as needed to thin chili to desired consistency.
  • Stir in kidney beans and pinto beans during the last 15 minutes of cooking.
  • Let chili cool slightly and serve with toppings of choice.

Notes

*If you want a slightly spicy chili sometimes I also like to include 1/2 to 1 tsp chipotle chili powder in addition to the other two types.
**If you don't want to include the alcohol simply increase chicken broth by 1/2 cup. **If you need to make this gluten free be sure not to use beer as it is derived from barley/wheat and is not gluten free.
Great Topping Options (pick as many as you'd like)
Cheddar, Monterey Jack or Pepper Jack cheese, cooked bacon, sour cream, red onion or green onion, avocados, charred corn, tortilla chips or saltine crackers, thinly sliced jalapenos, cornbread croutons, cilantro, lime wedges.
